taxonomic_note: Species-level learner target. Hill Country material is strongly represented by var. pubescens; do not assign variety from appearance alone without specimen/source support.
look_here_first: Look for narrow linear leaflets plus a dense swollen cylindrical-to-ovoid head. If the real question is D. compacta versus D. purpurea, move immediately to the calyx.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Barneby's native Hill Country var. pubescens treatment cites Hays (Barneby 14503), Blanco (14500) and Kerr (Heller 1857). Purola's introduced-site record is excluded.

best_field_traits: few pairs of narrow linear to linear-elliptic leaflets
very dense terminal ovoid/oblong/cylindrical flower head
D. purpurea separation depends strongly on calyx characters
morphology_keys.habit: Clumping herbaceous perennial from thick root/short caudex.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Few pairs of narrow linear to linear-elliptic leaflets; var. pubescens commonly under 3 mm wide.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Very dense swollen ovoid, oblong or cylindrical/conelike head.
morphology_keys.calyx: Priority structure for separation from D. purpurea; use size and external pubescence pattern rather than flower color.

comparisons.key_distinctions: D. purpurea can be very similar vegetatively; confirm with calyx characters. D. aurea is much silkier. D. enneandra has a loose spike with exposed rachis.

photo_note: CC0 species-level candidate recorded; variety should not be inferred from the image.
